title: AIS Stationary-Vessel Drift Watch
dataSources: Battery telemetry (`marine:battery`), AIS traffic (`marine:ais`), shore power (`marina:power`), tide forecasts (`tide:table`), export syncs (`marine:export`).
app: Boating and marine telemetry — Victron BMV battery exports, AIS transponder logs, shore-power meter readings, and NOAA tide tables — streamed to Splunk HEC via NMEA exports and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=marine:ais anchorage=* drift_alert=*
| stats count as total, sum(eval(if(drift_alert="yes",1,0))) as matched by anchorage
| eval a_drift_alert_pct=round(100*matched/total,1)
| sort - a_drift_alert_pct
description: Measures the percentage of stationary-vessel intervals that end with a drift alert by anchorage.
value: Completion and exception percentages make it easier to spot which anchorage are helping or hurting stationary-vessel intervals.
implementation: Store a normalized flag for `a drift alert` on `marine:ais` events and summarize the hit rate by `anchorage`.
visualization: Table of anchorage with percentage of stationary-vessel intervals ending with a drift alert.
grandmaExplanation: It gathers how often a drift alert happens for each anchorage so you can see where stationary-vessel intervals go smoothly or get stuck.
